passage:
I'm Vidya, and last week I sighed the loudest in maths. Jomon was stuck on the same fraction sum for ages, tapping his pencil and staring. I finished mine, then whispered, "It's so easy!" and rolled my eyes. Jomon's ears went red.
Our teacher walked over to Jomon and didn't sigh. She drew the sum as a chocolate bar and waited while he tried. When Jomon got it, she just nodded, as if it hadn't taken long at all.
My face went warm. The next day I said, "Do you want to see how I did it?" and Jomon did.

qa.q: What sum was Jomon stuck on?
qa.a: The same fraction sum, for ages.

qa.q: What did Vidya feel when watching the teacher help Jomon?
qa.a: Vidya felt embarrassed. The warm face shows that Vidya realised the sighs and eye-rolling were unkind.

qa.q: What choice did Vidya make the next day?
qa.a: Vidya offered to show Jomon how Vidya had done the sum, instead of sighing.

qa.q: How might Jomon have felt when Vidya whispered 'It's so easy!'?
qa.a: Embarrassed and hurt, since Jomon's ears went red.

grounding: A quick child sighs at a slower classmate's struggle and learns patience by watching a teacher deal with slowness kindly.

passage:
Note from Sabina, class 4 teacher. During fractions today Sudha finished early, then sighed loudly each time Ravi paused over his sum, and finally muttered, "Hurry up." Ravi stopped writing and looked at his desk. I did not scold her in front of the class.
At break I asked Sudha to help me draw a number line for everyone, and told her it took me a long time to learn it too. She was quiet. Later I overheard her say to Ravi, "You can borrow my ruler."
I will pair them on Thursday and keep modelling patience. Sudha is quick, but she has not yet seen that people move at different speeds.

qa.q: What did Sudha mutter to Ravi?
How might Ravi have felt when Sudha sighed and muttered?
qa.a: Embarrassed and pressured. He stopped writing and looked at his desk.

qa.q: What did Sabina do instead of scolding Sudha in front of the class?
qa.a: Sabina asked Sudha to help draw a number line and said it took Sabina a long time to learn it too, showing that pace differs.

qa.q: What does Sabina think Sudha has not yet understood?
qa.a: That people move at different speeds. Sudha is quick but has not yet seen how slower classmates feel.

grounding: A quick child sighs at a slower classmate's struggle, and an adult models patience.
